name: @agent-lcars/dispatch-broker
// why: The source lives here rather than under .github/actions because that directory is deployment surface: it holds action.yml and the committed bundle this target produces, and nothing else. Keeping the source in a normal Nx app is what gives it lint, typecheck, test and build targets on the same terms as every other project. #1015 Wave 4 deleted .github/actions/dispatch-broker (its last live use, the Claude-lane-readiness probe, was retired) and .github/actions/deliverable-watchdog, so their `build`/`build-deliverable-watchdog` targets went too -- see apps/dispatch-broker/README.md for why this app itself is kept: apps/console's hosted-controller.ts still imports main.ts/normalize.ts/storage/services as a library for the console-triggered Retry/Reassign-pipeline commands, and build-rerun-infra-killed-runs below still produces the externally-published rerun-infra-killed-runs bundle.

test.// why: workflow-contract.spec.ts reads .github/workflows/*.yml at runtime, so those files are real inputs to this target even though nothing imports them. Without declaring them, Nx hashes only this project's own sources and happily serves a cached pass after a workflow changes -- meaning the suite whose entire job is catching workflow drift would be the one thing that never notices it. Verified: editing a worker workflow used to leave `pnpm nx test` green from cache.

build-rerun-infra-killed-runs.// why: Same committed-dependency-free-bundle pattern as `build` above, for the sibling rerun-infra-killed-runs action. rerun-infra-killed-runs/main.mjs used to import ../dispatch-broker/github-api.mjs directly, a path #695 deleted; that broke this action outright (five straight scheduled-run failures, silently killing the self-healing path that reruns infra-killed CI runs) with nothing to catch it. This target plus the drift check in ci.yml is the fix.
